errors.text: The hypothesis assigns loss of small particles primarily to Ostwald ripening and predicts growth of the average particle size, whereas the target mechanism emphasizes Au/Cu surface segregation followed by melting and evaporation, producing an approximately 22% size reduction.
It predicts increasingly non-spherical, anisotropic particles, contrary to the observed elliptical-to-spherical reshaping with temperature.
It identifies only Au as the relevant low-surface-energy segregant and omits the central role of Cu segregation and Au/Cu evaporation.
